excerpt: Prepare for an off-plan handover in Ras Al Khaimah with a practical document, inspection and payment checklist.
introduction:
An off-plan handover is more than collecting keys. The buyer needs to check the completion notice, contract, outstanding payments, condition of the unit and the process for recording defects. Start preparing before the appointment and keep a written record of each step.

The timing and remedies depend on the signed documents and the current requirements for the property.
takeaways: Read the notice and contract before making the final payment or signing acceptance.
Inspect the unit against the signed plan and specifications and record defects with dates.
Confirm registration, utilities, management, insurance and access before occupation or letting.

sections.heading: Before the appointment
sections.body:
Read the signed sale agreement, payment schedule, approved plans and specification alongside the developer's handover notice. Check what must be paid, the deadline, the documents required and whether the contract provides an inspection before acceptance. Ask for a written breakdown of any adjustments, service charges or other amounts.

Confirm the unit number, floor, parking and storage allocated to you. If you cannot attend, ask the developer what authority and identification a representative needs. Do not assume an advertising image or model unit forms part of the contract: compare the completed property with the documents that actually apply.

table.caption: Handover evidence checklist
rows: Signed plan, specifications, notices and payment schedule
Dated photographs and written snag list
Current ownership record and required transfer documents
Keys, access, utility and building rules

sections.heading: Arrange the right inspection
sections.body:
Visit in daylight if possible and allow enough time to inspect each room and the common areas relevant to access. A qualified snagging inspector can help assess workmanship and operating systems; an independent technical specialist may be appropriate for a significant concern. Agree their scope and fee in advance.

Check dimensions against the contractual basis, doors, windows, paint, flooring, joinery, appliances and water fixtures. Test cooling, lights and sockets where safe and permitted. Examine the balcony and any assigned parking space. Note meter readings and photograph each issue with enough context to identify its location.

Before accepting an appointment date, confirm which utilities will be operating so the inspector can test the relevant systems. Ask whether the developer has a standard snag form and whether the same record will be used for the follow-up visit. Keep copies outside the developer's portal as well as in your email.

sections.heading: Document defects and remedies
sections.body:
Prepare a numbered list with a clear description, location, photograph and date. Send it through the developer's prescribed channel and ask for acknowledgement, the proposed repair date and a contact. Keep copies of notices, correspondence and the condition record. A verbal assurance is difficult to track if the person handling the case changes.

Ask whether a follow-up inspection is available and how unresolved items are escalated. Read the agreement before signing a handover or acceptance form: the implications of signing depend on the document and applicable law. If a serious dispute arises, seek independent legal advice on the specific facts.

sections.heading: Check payment and registration
sections.body:
Match each requested payment to the contract and independently verify the beneficiary details. Retain official receipts and reconcile previous instalments so a deposit or payment is not counted twice. For the registered sale process, [RAK Municipality's service](https://sanad.mun.rak.ae/docs/en/services-card-arabic-temp-28) explains documentation and fees; ask the authority which current process applies to your unit.

Request the relevant registration or title evidence, any developer clearance and the final allocation of parking. If the purchase is financed, coordinate with the lender about its release conditions, registration and insurance. Handover of keys and registration of rights are distinct steps.

sections.heading: Budget beyond the final instalment
sections.body:
Assume a buyer owes a sample AED 100,000 final instalment, AED 12,000 in initial furnishing and AED 8,000 in move-in and connection expenses. The cash planned for these example items is AED 120,000 before a separate contingency. These example amounts show the final instalment, furnishing and move-in costs in one cash plan.

Request written quotes for the specific apartment, including any service charge due at handover. If furnishing for tenants, add replacements, utility deposits and an initial vacancy period. Keep a reserve that is not committed to the developer's final instalment.

chart.title: Example handover cash plan
chart.note: Sample amounts; excludes other fees and a separate contingency.

sections.heading: Set up the home
sections.body:
Ask who manages the building, how to obtain access cards and where to report urgent faults. Confirm utility connections, building insurance and the owner's own insurance needs. Collect appliance manuals, warranties, contact details and instructions for cooling, water and access systems.

Review rules for moving, contractors, pets, parking and alterations. Test keys and access cards before the appointment ends where practical. Ask how and when owners receive the service-charge budget and how maintenance requests are tracked. A completed apartment may still have common facilities undergoing separate works, so confirm their actual availability.

sections.heading: If you plan to rent
sections.body:
Record the move-in condition before a tenant occupies the home and agree who will handle marketing, maintenance and deposits. Use comparable signed leases, not an assumed headline return, when preparing a rental budget. Deduct vacancy, service charges, insurance and management.

For short stays, check the current permit and building rules. The [RAK Tourism holiday-home system update](https://raktda.com/press-release-ras-al-khaimah-tourism-development-authority-continues-to-diversify-tourism-offering-with-new-updates-to-its-rak-holiday-homes-system/) describes registration by owners and operators. Obtain current conditions and operator terms before taking bookings.

[ARN also reported the authority’s holiday-home registration update](https://www.arnnewscentre.ae/en/news/uae/ras-al-khaimah-simplifies-holiday-homes-system/). Verify current requirements directly with the authority.

sections.heading: Keep the handover file
sections.body:
Store the signed contract, payment receipts, inspection list, repair acknowledgements, warranty documents and final registration evidence together. Record who is responsible for each outstanding item and follow up in writing on the agreed dates. Review the contract and seek advice where the developer's response does not resolve a material problem.

Compare the [RAK area guide](/journal/ras-al-khaimah-property-lifestyle) with the actual building and its services. Browse [RAK projects](/projects?emirate=Ras%20Al%20Khaimah) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) for current project information. Verify the exact unit and official process before proceeding.
